name: Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA)
description: EU-wide licensing, conduct, and prudential framework for crypto-asset issuers and crypto-asset service providers (CASPs), including custody, white papers, asset-referenced tokens, and market-abuse controls.

modules.obligation: Entities providing crypto-asset services in the Union must obtain CASP authorisation from a competent authority before going live, unless a limited exemption applies. The application must describe the programme of operations, legal form, and intended services (including custody).
evidence_checklist: CASP authorisation application or equivalent passporting notice
programme of operations covering each intended crypto-asset service

modules.obligation: Offerings of crypto-assets (other than ART/EMT where specific titles apply) require a crypto-asset white paper with fair, clear, and not-misleading information on the issuer, the asset, rights, risks, and the underlying technology. Marketing must be consistent with the white paper.
evidence_checklist: MiCA-aligned white paper with required content headings
risk-factor section covering technology, liquidity, and legal risks
notification or publication record for the white paper

modules.obligation: Issuers of asset-referenced tokens must maintain a reserve of assets that matches the risks and composition of the referenced assets, keep the reserve segregated, and ensure it is not encumbered for the issuer's own obligations. Composition, valuation, and custody of the reserve must be documented.
evidence_checklist: independent attestation or audit of reserve holdings
segregation of reserve from issuer operating funds

modules.obligation: Holders of asset-referenced tokens must have a permanent right of redemption against the issuer at market value of the referenced assets, or by delivery of those assets, under published conditions that are not unduly restrictive.
evidence_checklist: operational process for holder redemption requests
disclosure of fees and conditions of redemption

modules.obligation: CASPs that hold client crypto-assets or funds must make adequate arrangements to safeguard ownership rights, keep client assets distinct from the firm's own, and prevent use of client assets for own account except with explicit consent. Funds should be placed with a credit institution or central bank where applicable.
evidence_checklist: consent records if any reuse of client assets is contemplated

modules.obligation: Providers of custody and administration of crypto-assets on behalf of clients must establish a custody policy, maintain a register of positions, keep client crypto-assets segregated on the distributed ledger or by other equivalent means, and exercise due care over control of cryptographic keys.
evidence_checklist: on-chain segregation or equivalent control evidence

modules.obligation: CASPs must identify, prevent, manage and disclose conflicts of interest between themselves (including managers, employees and shareholders) and their clients, and among clients. Organisational arrangements and disclosures must be proportionate to the services offered.
evidence_checklist: governance chart for the management body

modules.obligation: Authorised CASPs must hold prudential safeguards equal to the higher of a permanent minimum capital amount or a fraction of fixed overheads, in the form of own funds or an equivalent insurance policy covering the territories where services are provided.
evidence_checklist: own-funds calculation vs. minimum capital / overheads
insurance policy if used as a safeguard

modules.obligation: CASPs must establish and maintain effective, transparent procedures for prompt handling of client complaints, publish those procedures, keep records of complaints and remedies, and ensure clients can file free of charge in an official language of the home Member State or of the client's location.

Persons professionally arranging or executing transactions in crypto-assets must have arrangements to detect and report insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information, and market manipulation. Issuers and CASPs must control inside information and maintain proportionate surveillance.

CASPs must have robust governance arrangements, including a clear organisational structure, effective risk-management and internal-control mechanisms, business-continuity plans, and ICT security commensurate with the scale of crypto-asset services.

Where a CASP outsources operational functions, it remains fully responsible to clients and competent authorities. Outsourcing must not impair internal control, competent-authority supervision, or the quality of services. Material outsourcing requires due diligence, written agreements, and exit plans.
evidence_checklist: written agreements with key-management / cloud providers
exit and contingency plans for custody infrastructure
